title: Stand with Jensen Site
gist: SemiWiki's Daniel Nenni shares the 'Stand with Jensen' petition site, which asks Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO after his November 12, 2026 resignation pending an independent investigation, and to explain its decision; the site claimed ~194,000 self-reported, unverified signatures as of November 17.

themes.theme: Nvidia CEO exit and governance shock

insights.claim: Nvidia announced on November 12, 2026 that Jensen Huang resigned as CEO effective immediately, ending 33 years leading the company he co-founded.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: An abrupt founder-CEO exit at the most important AI chip company is a major key-person and governance risk event for NVDA holders.
insights.quote: On November 12, 2026, NVIDIA announced that Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, effective immediately.

insights.claim: According to the petition, an outside investigation into Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia has been announced but has not concluded, and signers say they have seen no evidence substantiating the allegation that a woman at the center of the controversy was a spy.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The investigation outcome is the key catalyst; watch for its scope, timeline and findings as a binary event for leadership continuity.
insights.quote: We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy.
insights.locator: Our understanding is that an outside

insights.claim: Petition organizers worry Jensen Huang may have been forced out of Nvidia without due process and without even a few days to make his case.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Perceived lack of due process can fuel employee, shareholder and partner backlash, raising pressure on the board.

insights.claim: The Stand with Jensen open letter asks Nvidia's board to take three actions: reinstate Huang while an independent investigation establishes the facts, guarantee an independent inquiry with a fair hearing and disclosed scope and timeline, and provide a timely public explanation of the evidence and how employee and shareholder interests were weighed.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: These are the concrete asks to track against board communications; any concession signals the board's position is softening.
insights.locator: We ask the Board to take

insights.claim: The petition argues that suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen Huang's leadership of Nvidia and that the inquiry must establish facts rather than justify an outcome already imposed.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Frames the governance dispute as process legitimacy, which shapes how institutional holders may vote or engage.
insights.quote: Suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen's leadership.
insights.locator: Our understanding is that an outside

insights.claim: Signers of the Stand with Jensen letter describe themselves as current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, and credit Huang with betting the company on ideas most of the industry dismissed.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals potential internal morale and talent-retention risk if employees strongly identify with the departed founder.

insights.claim: As of November 17, 2026 the Stand with Jensen site displayed roughly 194,000 signatures, a campaign-reported count whose signer affiliations are self-reported and unverified.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signature counts gauge public sentiment but are unverified; treat as a soft indicator of pressure on the board.
insights.quote: As of November 17, the site displayed roughly 194,000 signatures.

insights.claim: The Stand with Jensen campaign says it is volunteer-run and not affiliated with or endorsed by Nvidia or Huang, while the Wall Street Journal reported that an Nvidia employee built the site using Replit.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Employee involvement suggests internal dissent with the board's decision, a cultural risk to monitor.
insights.quote: The Wall Street Journal reported that an Nvidia employee built the site using Replit.
insights.locator: The campaign describes itself as volunteer-run
